A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CBDebug research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C are readable and can be reliably matched, including relocated passages and renumbered tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments with human and automated concept feedback, including six user debugging sessions, numerical results in Tables 1-2, and additional analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports augmentation-exponent sensitivity results for Post-hoc CBM on Waterbirds in Appendix C.3, Table 8.

M1.justification: The removal-and-retraining framework, auxiliary-label construction, permutation weighting, and CutMix/Mixup augmentation remain unchanged. The expanded augmentation description and explicit task-level scope clarify the existing procedure rather than introduce a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Waterbirds, MetaShift, CelebA, and ISIC with the same human-feedback and automated-feedback task coverage. The new augmentation-exponent sweep uses the existing Waterbirds task and does not introduce another dataset, population, or test scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1-2 and Appendix C.4: removal, standard retraining, ProtoPDebug where applicable, component ablations, and JTT/LfF remain in their corresponding comparisons. v1 Table 8 becomes v2 Table 9 without changing the comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a downstream accuracy evaluation varying the augmentation exponent over gamma = 1, 2, 5, and 10. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged; gamma = 2 generally and gamma = 5 for ISIC were already documented in v1 Appendix A.3.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix C.3 only displayed augmentation-probability histograms and stated that gamma = 2 worked well. v2 adds an accuracy sensitivity study testing whether performance depends on the exponent. Existing permutation-weighting ablations and concept visualizations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions already report means and standard deviations over three initial seeds or six debugging sessions. The new sensitivity table adds plus/minus result entries without introducing a different uncertainty-reporting practice, new run-count information, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: New Table 8 adds average and worst-group accuracy results for gamma = 1, 5, and 10, with worst-group accuracies of 60.2 ± 12.7, 58.9 ± 9.1, and 62.5 ± 11.4, respectively. Its gamma = 2 row repeats Table 2's existing results. Previously reported numerical results and concept examples remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical CBM formulation, auxiliary-label construction, and permutation-weight equation are unchanged. Appendix A.4 supplies verbal explanations of existing terms. The task-level qualification clarifies the existing feedback model without introducing a new formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a general removal-and-retraining framework, CBDebug's conversion of concept feedback into sample-level supervision, and empirical benefits across CBM architectures and feedback sources.

C2.justification: New Section 7 explicitly discusses performance variability, dependence on accurate feedback, and inability to directly address class-specific spuriosity; Section 3.2 also clarifies the task-level restriction. Appendix C.3 interprets the new sweep as evidence of gamma robustness and explains the existing ISIC setting as limiting augmentation-induced distribution shifts.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 now explicitly specifies random sampling of the Mixup image from the selected concept's image bank. This is a limited implementation clarification. The top-ten patch sampling rule, training settings, hardware, code-access information, and default gamma values were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chauhan et al. and Hu et al. to the debugging discussion, clarifies the class-specific versus task-specific scope of earlier approaches, and adds healthcare-motivation citations to Makary and Daniel and Lekadir et al. The overall positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands the augmentation description into architecture-specific bullets, adds a short Limitations section and Definitions subsection, and updates cross-references, related-work prose, and acknowledgements. These are localized edits within the retained document structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds the augmentation sensitivity table in Appendix C.3 and renumbers the existing unsupervised-baseline table from 8 to 9. Existing figures and table structures are retained, with local placement and page-flow changes accompanying the added text.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens the paper by supplementing v1's informal gamma choice with quantitative sensitivity evidence and explicitly acknowledging variability, feedback dependence, and task-level applicability limits. Clarified implementation and related work improve transparency. The added evidence remains confined to one model-dataset combination with substantial variability, so it supports a limited improvement rather than a substantial strengthening of the unchanged main results.
